label: input h at original-phase positions 4-7
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, when the input token is the letter h at position t = 4..7. On the dev split every such step fires (precision 1.0). It never fires on h at positions 0-3, only weakly and rarely at t=8 (102 steps, about 0% of mass), and never on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (including when h is fed back as a copied output). Magnitude is highest at t=5-6 and lower at t=4 and t=7. It is much weaker when h already appeared shortly before (e.g. a second h right after an h at t=6 gave 0.06 of max), and weaker in shorter sequences where the h is far from the delimiter.

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.997, F1 0.9987 and mass recall 0.9997, with 0 false positives.

The only misses are 104 test steps, all at t=8 with input h (L=9) and weak activations (0.03-0.10 of max, about 0% of mass). This is the weak t=8 tail the explanation already describes. Adding t==8 to the predicate would hurt it: alone, that predicate has precision 0.037.

The profile confirms the remaining claims: the feature never fires in the delimiter or copy phase (even when the output token is h), on any token other than h, or at t<=3. Mass per active step is highest at t=5-6.

The claims about weaker activation after a recent h, and weaker activation by L/to_go, are magnitude claims only. The explanation already flags them as not directly checked, and they do not affect the label.
